text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: page fired - ALERT: alb-target-health-unhealthy (eu-west-1) - 401 users affected, increased 502/524 errors. runbook: /runbooks/network-alb-targets.md

Alex P: acked. I'm oncall for infra. Looking at ALB in eu-west-1 now.

Maria L: on it too, checking recent deploys + cert rotation earlier this morning. Any correlation with the 08:12 deploy?

Alex P: I see target group tg-frontend-eu: 60% targets unhealthy, health check failing with TLS handshake error in ALB logs.

Sam G: saw customer 502s in logs as well, traces show frontend->backend TLS handshake failures, but backend pods are up. Could be ALB cipher mismatch or security policy change.

Jordan H: paging summary from PagerDuty: CI=Critical, started 1902345600, metric: target_group_unhealthy_count > 30 for 5m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC12345

Alex P: Running AWS CLI to inspect:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-frontend-eu/abcdef
```
Response shows HealthDescriptions with reason: TLS handshake failure.

Maria L: confirmed cert rotation job ran at 08:10, but it was for edge certs on CloudFront, not ALB. However there was a change to ALB security policy via terraform earlier (tls-policy=ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017 -> stricter policy). Could be new policy incompatible with some backend NGINX.

Sam G: quick check to backend NGINX logs: `ssl_protocol_version` shows TLSv1.2 and some client cipher negotiation failures. Backends are nginx 1.18, using OpenSSL 1.1.1.

Jordan H: Impact: external customers in EU hitting app via ALB receive intermittent 502/524s. Some routes affected more (upload endpoints). Severity: P2->P1 if >10% traffic impacted. Current estimate ~3-5% but trending up.

Alex P: Mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily set ALB security policy back to previous permissive one (rollback terraform) to restore handshakes. 2) As fallback, failover traffic to eu-west-1 standby cluster behind an NLB that uses TCP (no TLS termination) and let backend handle TLS. Which is faster?

Maria L: Rolling back ALB policy is fastest. I'll make the change manually in console to avoid terraform apply drift. Alex, want me to do that?

Alex P: Yes please. Also we should throttle migration window, set small batch. I'll open a console change and notify.

Maria L: making change now: changing security policy from ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2021 to ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017 (temporary).

incident-bot: system: configuration change detected by monitor for alb/app/frontend-alb/50dc6c495c0c9188.

Sam G: I can tail the access logs to see handshake success: `aws s3 cp s3://alb-logs/eu-west-1/2026/05/` and grep TLS.

Maria L: change applied. Waiting 30s for targets to re-evaluate.

Alex P: monitoring target health...

Jordan H: customer comms: I'll draft a short status update for status.redwood.in: "Partial outage in EU region affecting some requests; mitigation in progress, will update in 30m."

Alex P: target health improving: 60% -> 95% healthy in last 45s. Application 200s recovering, error rate dropping.

Sam G: confirmed reduced 502s on traces, upload endpoints show successful TLS handshakes again.

Maria L: note: we're leaving the permissive policy until we coordinate a safer migration. Action item: research backend cipher support and update nginx/OpenSSL.

Alex P: I'll create a follow-up ticket to harden: ticket #INFRA-7123 with rollback details and next steps to reintroduce stricter policy after backend update.

Jordan H: posted status update v1 to status page and pinged account managers for top 5 customers in EU.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by Alex P at 1902345700.

Maria L: handoff: I'll stay on for 30m to verify stability, then hand back to Alex for overnight.

Alex P: thanks. Summary for postmortem: cause = ALB security policy tightened; effect = TLS handshake failures for some backend OpenSSL versions; mitigation = manual rollback to previous ALB policy; follow-up = update backend OpenSSL/NGINX and automate policy rollout testing.

Jordan H: closing loop: error rate back to baseline for 8 minutes. I'll close PagerDuty once stable for 15m.

Alex P: handing to oncall for platform monitoring (Jordan) at 1902346030. Please escalate if any regression. :thumbsup:
